clue.text: Bachelor with girl spotted handkerchief

parts.note: with means and, joining two things
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A single man takes a young woman out, and she ends up with a polka-dot hanky.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly coloured kerchief, typically with white spots, worn round the neck or head.

clue.text: Golf shot is near

definitions.meaning: a stroke played onto the green from the fairway
a verb phrase: to draw close, come nearer

explanation.surface: A golfer's ball lands close to the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The stroke hit towards the green is named for drawing close, and as a verb the word means to come close to something.

clue.text: Host shows trick with some cards

definitions.meaning: a verb: to act as host, serve drinks or carve the meat
at bridge, winning a trick by playing the honour cards (ace, king, queen, jack, ten)

explanation.surface: A party host entertains the guests with a card trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link joining the two definitions. The honours are the top cards of a suit at bridge, so the second reading jokes about taking a trick with them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to perform the duties of a host, such as pouring drinks; read literally it is playing one's top court cards.

clue.text: We hear rough play is forbidden by this declaration

indicators.note: signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to tromp is to stamp or trample heavily, so a ban on rough play is no tromps

explanation.surface: Someone announces a rule banning roughhousing.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge, a contract played without a trump suit is announced as a bid; the clue says it sounds like a ban on tromping about.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a bid naming no trump suit is a call made in the auction.

clue.text: A tree in the garden appearing red

indicators.note: the tree word is placed inside the garden word, as plants sit in a bed

parts.note: a flower bed is part of the garden
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree in the garden glows red in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing red' is the definition, a blushing face, not autumn leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, so their face goes red.

clue.text: Old wood surrounding hollow

indicators.note: the small wood is placed around the abbreviation for old

parts.note: a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: An ancient forest encircles a dip in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow channel or furrow cut into a surface is a hollow.

clue.text: Explorer who wrote masses

definitions.meaning: Richard ..., the American polar explorer and aviator
William ..., the Tudor composer of three famous Masses

explanation.surface: A traveller who also produced a great deal of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masses' looks like 'lots', but it is the church music, the Mass settings of the Elizabethan composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two famous men share the surname: an American polar aviator and an English Renaissance church composer.

clue.text: Help to put out fire, in turn

indicators.note: the scrambled fire is placed inside the word for turn

parts.note: a bend is a turn in a road

indicators.note: put out here means disturbed or upset, so the letters of fire are jumbled

explanation.surface: A firefighter is told to help extinguish a blaze, taking turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' suggests extinguishing; it is the anagram signal, making FRIE, which goes inside BEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a friend to someone, giving support, is to help them.

clue.text: Surrender in US ordered by our General, in short — this one

definitions.text: Surrender in US ordered by our General, in short — this one

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: Gen is the short form of General

explanation.surface: A British commander capitulated in America, and here he is.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange BY, OUR and GEN. General John Burgoyne surrendered the British army at Saratoga in 1777, during the American War of Independence, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The British general who capitulated at Saratoga is the man whose surrender in America the clue describes.

clue.text: Eggs ejected from mouth

definitions.meaning: the spawn of oysters and other shellfish

explanation.surface: Someone spits out a mouthful of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyster spawn shares its name with the past tense of the verb for expelling saliva.

clue.text: Uncomfortable place to cry, but it's there if you break down

definitions.meaning: one cries on someone's shoulder; an unsympathetic one is a hard one

definitions.text: it's there if you break down
definitions.meaning: the emergency lane on a motorway where a broken-down car can stop

explanation.surface: An unsympathetic friend is little use when you collapse in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break down' reads as weeping, but it is a car failing: the hard shoulder is the strip beside a British motorway for stopping in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: An unyielding body part offers poor comfort to someone weeping, and the paved roadside strip is where stranded motorists pull over.

clue.text: Shepherdess's brief game of hide-and-seek

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: brief means short, little
bo-peep is a game of hiding and peeping out to amuse a baby

explanation.surface: A shepherdess plays a quick round of hide-and-seek.
explanation.walkthrough: She is the nursery-rhyme girl who lost her sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme character who lost her flock is the best-known shepherdess in children's verse.

clue.text: Understand in depth

definitions.meaning: to comprehend, get to the bottom of
a unit of six feet used for measuring the depth of water

explanation.surface: A plea to comprehend something thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to grasp a problem, and the noun is a nautical depth measure of six feet.

clue.text: I have chosen to go first — it's optional

indicators.note: the word for chosen is placed in front of the other piece

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone claims first turn, saying it's up to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A course or procedure that is not compulsory is chosen at will, so optional.

clue.text: Wine comes in his 'n' her varieties

indicators.note: varieties suggests different versions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wine marketed in matching versions for couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock and other white wines from the Rhine region are called by this adjective.

clue.text: Hard Times as a serial, say?

definitions.text: Hard Times as a serial, say?

parts.words: Hard Times as a serial, say?
parts.note: Hard Times, the Dickens novel, appeared in instalments

explanation.surface: Dickens's novel Hard Times published in instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard times is a rough age; a serial sounds like cereal, the breakfast food rich in fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran and cereal fibre is what this word means, and the clue splits it into a difficult era.

clue.text: Cut back dripping tree with its crown removed

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off branches
dripping is fat from roasting meat, like lard

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts back a wet tree, removing its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dripping' looks like wet; it is cooking fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree whose upper branches have been cut back to the trunk to encourage dense new growth.

clue.text: I love the sun — terrible what it can do to the moon

definitions.text: what it can do to the moon

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters are badly mixed up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sunbather loves the sun, but thinks it's awful how it eclipses the moon's light.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun is so bright that it makes the moon look dim by comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: To be brighter than something is to eclipse it, as the sun does to the moon by day.

clue.text: Soldiers' fighting response

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
action is fighting, as in seeing action

explanation.surface: The troops respond by fighting back.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply or answer to a stimulus is a response.

clue.text: Peculiarity half the cardinals show

definitions.meaning: half of the cardinal numbers, 1, 3, 5 and so on, are odd ones

explanation.surface: Half the College of Cardinals behave strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen; it means the cardinal numbers, half of which are odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangeness is a peculiarity, and it is also the quality of being not divisible by two.

clue.text: In casual dress, not being fit

explanation.surface: Someone dressed down is turned away as unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing no formal suit, and also unsuitable for a purpose or role.

clue.text: Black Watch coming round the wood

indicators.note: the word for watch goes around the letter for black

parts.note: a timer is a clock or watch
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The Black Watch regiment come through the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Watch is a famous Scottish infantry regiment, but here the words separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber cut from trees is wood used for building.

clue.text: Apocryphal character who found a theatrical angel

definitions.text: Apocryphal character who found a theatrical angel

parts.words: Apocryphal character who found a theatrical angel
parts.note: a figure from the Book of Tobit who meets the archangel Raphael, a story later staged by James Bridie as a play

explanation.surface: A biblical figure who discovered a backer for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatrical angel is a show's financial backer; here the angel is literally Raphael in Bridie's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of Tobit in the Apocrypha travels with the archangel Raphael, the subject of a well-known 1930 stage play.

clue.text: How to get away with an old chestnut?

definitions.text: How to get away with an old chestnut?

parts.words: How to get away with an old chestnut?
parts.note: chestnut is read as a brown horse, not a tired joke; riding off on one takes skill

explanation.surface: Advice on telling a stale joke without groans.
explanation.walkthrough: An old chestnut is a hackneyed joke; a chestnut is also a reddish-brown horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in riding is what lets one ride off on a horse.

clue.text: Our crumbling drive at last gets a rake

indicators.note: crumbling signals that the letters fall apart and are rearranged
takes the final letter of drive

explanation.surface: A crumbling driveway is cleared with a garden rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool; it is a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A debauched, pleasure-seeking man is called a rake.

clue.text: Superior companion, chosen from a series

indicators.note: the letters are picked from within the words a series

explanation.surface: A top-quality colleague selected from a range of candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Superior and its neighbour are two of North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Great Lakes, it sits next to Lake Superior.

clue.text: GUM store ransacked by those seeking a good table

indicators.note: a ransacked shop has its contents thrown about

explanation.surface: Diners looking for good food raid a chewing-gum shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Connoisseurs of fine food look for restaurants that keep a good table.

clue.text: Jo's work at the crossing ends finally in tears

indicators.note: takes the last letter of ends

parts.note: weeping means crying, in tears

explanation.surface: A tearful ending for a character in a sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo is the crossing sweeper in Dickens's Bleak House, whose death is famously tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Jo's job in Bleak House was clearing a street crossing with a broom.
